# **2\. Multimodal PDF Ingestion Architecture**

Version 1 treats PDFs primarily as sources of extractable text. Version 2 should preserve the working text pipeline while adding page-level processing for tables and visual content. To keep the project achievable, the architecture converts heterogeneous PDF content into a common text-based, provenance-aware representation before embedding it with the existing text embedding model.

| PDF Upload    |    v Document Loader    |    v Page-by-Page PDF Processor    |    \+--\> Text \--------------------\> text extraction    |    \+--\> Tables \------------------\> structured table extraction    |    \+--\> Images / Diagrams \-------\> vision analysis    |    \+--\> Charts \------------------\> vision \+ fact extraction    |    v Normalized Document Elements (content \+ type \+ document \+ page \+ element ID)    |    v Content-Aware Chunking    |    v all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Embeddings    |    v ChromaDB    |    v Existing Hybrid Retrieval \-\> Gemini \-\> Answer |
| :---- |

# **3\. Representation Strategy by PDF Content Type**

| Content Type | Extraction | RAG Representation | Key Metadata |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Text** | Reuse/refactor existing PDF text extraction. | Paragraph/sentence-aware text chunks. | Document, page, section, element ID |
| **Tables** | Extract rows, columns, headers, captions, and cell relationships where possible. | Structured text or Markdown-like representation that preserves row/column meaning. | Document, page, table ID, caption |
| **Images / Diagrams** | Extract visual asset and send it to a vision-capable model for interpretation. | Searchable textual description plus important entities, relationships, labels, and facts. | Document, page, visual ID, model/method |
| **Charts** | Analyze chart title, labels, legend, values, trends, and comparisons. | Fact-oriented textual representation containing values and meaningful chart conclusions. | Document, page, chart ID, model/method |

# **4\. Multimodal Design Considerations**

* PDF processing library: prototype page/image/table extraction with representative project PDFs before selecting the final library.  
* Vision model/provider: evaluate a vision-capable model for diagrams, images, and charts; keep the implementation behind a reusable visual processor abstraction.  
* Table strategy: preserve structure instead of flattening cells into an unordered text stream.  
* Chunking: replace blind 800-character splitting for multimodal elements with content-aware boundaries; keep a maximum size for ordinary text.  
* Duplicate content: determine how to handle a chart plus a caption or paragraph that repeats the same facts.  
* Failure handling: one failed table/image extraction should be logged without preventing the rest of the PDF from being ingested.  
* Provenance: every retrieved element should retain its source document, page number, content type, and extraction method.

# **4\. V2.0 Chunking Strategy**

Version 2.0 will replace the fixed 800-character chunking strategy with a lightweight structure-aware approach. Document Elements will be chunked according to their content type. Normal text will be grouped using paragraph boundaries and, when necessary, sentence boundaries while respecting a configurable maximum chunk size. Large tables will be divided into logical row groups with column headers repeated across chunks, while concise chart, diagram, and image descriptions will generally remain intact. Overlap will occur at meaningful paragraph or sentence boundaries rather than at arbitrary character positions. This approach improves contextual integrity while remaining simple to implement, understand, and evaluate against the Version 1 baseline.

# **5\. Conversation Context Architecture**

The conversation-memory deliverable should focus on maintaining context within an active conversation rather than building long-term personal memory. The system should persist each user and assistant turn, retrieve an appropriate amount of recent history, and use that history to interpret follow-up questions before retrieval and generation.

| Conversation    |    \+--\> User Message 1    |    \+--\> Assistant Message 1    |    \+--\> User Message 2 ("What GPA do they need?")    |    v Context Builder    |    \+--\> Recent conversation history    \+--\> Current user question    |    v Context-Aware Retrieval / Query Interpretation    |    v Retrieved Evidence    |    v Gemini    |    v Assistant Message 2    |    v Persist Message |
| :---- |

# **6\. Conversation and Message Storage Design**

| Entity | Purpose | Suggested Fields |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **conversations** | Represents one chat session/thread. | conversation\_id, title/name, created\_at, updated\_at, status |
| **conversation\_messages** | Stores each turn in order. | message\_id, conversation\_id, role, content, sequence/created\_at |
| **message\_response link** | Associates an assistant turn with existing RAG response/provenance records. | message\_id, response\_id or equivalent foreign key |

The initial implementation should use a bounded recent-history strategy or a query-rewriting/context-building step rather than sending an unlimited conversation to the model.

# **7\. Proposed Version 2 Database Changes**

The exact table and column names should be finalized only after reviewing the current Version 1 schema. The following represents the intended data model rather than a final migration.

| Area | Proposed Change | Why | V1 Compatibility |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Document/chunk provenance** | Add page number, content type, element ID, and extraction method/model where appropriate. | Allows the system to identify whether evidence came from text, a table, chart, image, or diagram. | Existing text chunks can use content\_type='text' and nullable new fields. |
| **Conversations** | Add a conversations table. | Creates a persistent unit for each chat thread. | New table; no need to alter existing evaluation runs. |
| **Messages** | Add a conversation\_messages table linked to conversations. | Preserves ordered user/assistant turns for context. | New table; assistant messages can reference existing response records. |
| **RAG response linkage** | Link assistant messages to saved RAG responses/provenance. | Avoids duplicating existing answer/evidence storage. | Reuses the existing response/evaluation model where possible. |

# **10\. Initial Technology Stack**

For the first implementation, the simplest architecture is to keep the Version 1 technologies that already work and add only the capabilities required for multimodal extraction and conversation persistence.

| Component | Initial Choice |
| :---- | :---- |
| **PDF/page processing** | PyMuPDF |
| **Table extraction** | PyMuPDF find\_tables() first; test pdfplumber or Camelot as fallbacks |
| **Image/diagram/chart extraction** | PyMuPDF |
| **Visual understanding** | Gemini multimodal/image understanding |
| **Scanned-page fallback** | OCR only when a page has insufficient extractable text |
| **Normalized representation** | Simple Python DocumentElement dataclass |
| **Chunking** | Custom content-aware Python logic |
| **Embeddings** | Sentence Transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (reuse V1) |
| **Vector retrieval** | ChromaDB (reuse V1) |
| **Structured persistence** | MySQL (reuse V1) |
| **Conversation context** | MySQL message history \+ bounded Python context builder |
| **Testing** | pytest \+ existing evaluation framework |

## **PyMuPDF for PDF Processing**

PyMuPDF will serve as the primary PDF processing library for Version 2.0. It will open each PDF and process it page by page, allowing the system to extract standard text, identify and extract tables, locate embedded images, and render pages or visual regions when necessary. Text and tables that can be reliably extracted by PyMuPDF will be processed directly without requiring an AI model. PyMuPDF will also provide important provenance information, such as the source document and page number. The extracted information will then be converted into standardized **Document Elements**, such as text, table, chart, diagram, or image elements, before being chunked and indexed for retrieval.

## **Gemini for Image Classification and Understanding**

When PyMuPDF identifies significant visual content, such as an image, chart, or diagram, the visual will be passed to Gemini for interpretation. Gemini will first classify the visual to determine its type and whether it contains useful information. Informational visuals will then be analyzed to extract important text, labels, numerical values, relationships, trends, and other facts. Decorative or non-informational visuals, such as logos, can be excluded from the searchable knowledge base. Gemini's output will be converted into a textual representation and stored as a **Document Element**, allowing the existing text-based embedding and retrieval pipeline to search information that originally existed only in visual form.

## **Scanned PDF Fallback**

A scanned PDF may contain pages that appear to contain text but are actually stored as images, meaning normal PDF text extraction may return little or no usable text. Version 2.0 will use a fallback process when PyMuPDF detects this condition. The affected page will be rendered as an image and processed using **Optical Character Recognition (OCR)** to recover the written text. The recovered text can then be converted into a Document Element and processed through the normal chunking, embedding, and retrieval pipeline. OCR will only be used as a fallback when direct text extraction is insufficient, avoiding unnecessary processing of normal digital PDF pages.

## **Conversation History**

 Version 2.0 will use the existing MySQL database to persist conversations and individual user/assistant messages. A lightweight Python context manager will retrieve a bounded number of recent messages and provide them as context when processing follow-up questions. The existing PHP/JavaScript application will maintain the active conversation ID, while Gemini will use the supplied conversation context alongside retrieved document evidence to generate context-aware responses. No additional conversation-memory framework is required for the initial implementation.

# **11\. Technology Selection Criteria**

* Accuracy on the actual PDFs used by the project, especially tables and charts.  
* Ease of integration with the existing Python codebase.  
* Readable implementation that both team members can understand and maintain.  
* Ability to preserve page-level provenance.  
* Reasonable runtime and API cost during ingestion.  
* Backward compatibility with current TXT, DOCX, and text-based PDF behavior.
